newsitem.title: UK: T-bonds poised to shake off downturn, charts say.
newsitem.headline: T-bonds poised to shake off downturn, charts say.

text.p: U.S. T-bond futures are set to turn higher as cash yields are back in the buy zone and technicals chart a more positive course after weeks in the doldrums, technical analysts said.
"We've got the beginnings of early technical evidence supporting (a move up) and it's time to get involved," said Bill Westgate, vice-president at HSBC Securities here.
With the 30-year long bond offering yields around 7.10 percent, a lot of cash rich investors are poised to re-enter the market, analysts said. They just need a push.
The top of the recent range in the June T-bond future at 107-28 was the all-important watershed. ???
"The market could stretch higher, but it won't until it pushes through 107-28," said Elizabeth Miller, technical analyst at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell. "Then we could see it up a point."
Westgate agreed a lot of investors had been thinking about putting their money to work, once the market got to 107-25.
"So we're acutely sensitive of any price action that might be supportive at this point and we have begun to see this," he said.

The T-bond future has found the 107-28 level particularly hard to crack over the last few weeks. The market bounced off a high of 107-28 April 9, 107-27 on April 15 and 107-23 on Wednesday. By 1106 GMT it was up 8/32 at 107-23. The 30-year long bond was at 94-06, yielding 7.10 percent.

"But I think the trend is turning now and it will therefore now move into an uptrend," said Westgate, adding the fact the market bounced off its lows for the second day on Wednesday showed it was firmly rejecting lower levels.
A number of secondary technical indicators, useful in confirming any major technical price breaks, back up suggestions the mood in T-bonds has lightened lately, analysts said.
Stochastics -- or momentum indicators that suggest how much strength is behind a market move -- have turned bullish, said analysts.
"I agree that there is a buy signal given by modified stochastics," Miller said but the signal was not yet strong and was a subsidiary indicator, second to the price level.
Stavros Loizou, manager of strategic trading at Fuji Bank in London, also expected the market to move higher and agreed the main target was at 107-28.
"I would go with the upside," he said.
On the downside he saw good support at 106-29, Wednesday's low then at 106-23,24 the breakout point from the April 14 high.
Westgate said the relative strength index had put in a bullish divergence, which, with the stocastics, was supportive.
"Even in related markets -- gold is continuing to fall and that's not usually associated with bear market bonds and even utilities have managed to stem their losses," he said.
Not even the prospect of more U.S. rate rises should dampen sentiment, as these are already factored in, said Westgate.
"We've got three rate rises already priced in here. So if you're bearish from here you're betting on a fourth and a fifth rate hike coming in," said Westgate.
"They think rates should go to the moon but they don't realise we're already at the moon in terms of prices."
